requirements.text: If you find that more than three incidents are still ongoing, do not proceed with the suspension and instead update the service status to repair in progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_041' AND status = 'repair_in_progress'
assumptions: Office Printing resolves to SVC_041, the only service with that name; its seed status is operational

the branch fires: 9 incidents on SVC_041 are not resolved or closed (3 new, 3 in_progress, 3 on_hold, 4 resolved); 'active or in-progress' is read as not resolved or closed, since a reading that counts only status = in_progress gives exactly 3, which is not more than three, and the benchmark's check expects the branch to fire
'repair in progress' is the seed's status value repair_in_progress
not proceeding with the suspension is tested by this same cell: a retired or non-operational status would fail it
the acting user USER_039 is an admin, so no role rule blocks the service update

requirements.text: ensure that all related service offerings under this service are also updated to reflect the same status
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE business_service = 'SVC_041' AND status = 'repair_in_progress'
assumptions: the seed has one offering under SVC_041, SVCOFF_050 (Print Server - HQ), status operational, so the set count is 1; the original check anchors on that id and this selector picks out the same row

requirements.text: make sure the service owner is alerted immediately, referencing the high priority nature of the issue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_031' AND incident_id = 'INC_026' AND email = 'joanne.simpson@servicenow.com' AND type = 'alert'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest seed id NOTIF_030)
the service owner is SVC_041.owned_by = USER_004, Joanne Simpson, joanne.simpson@servicenow.com (active manager, ORG_001)

notification.incident_id is NOT NULL, so the alert must reference an incident; 'the high priority nature of the issue' is read as the high-priority ongoing incident on the service: INC_026 (high, in_progress, ORG_001) is the only high-priority incident on SVC_041 that is new or in_progress and the only one in the service's org; INC_068 (high, on_hold, ORG_007) is the alternative
'alerted' maps to type = alert, a seed enumeration value; the wording of subject and message is not tested

requirements.text: all related service offerings under this service (boundary: offerings of other services)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_offering WHERE business_service <> 'SVC_041' AND status = 'repair_in_progress'
assumptions: boundary of the 'related service offerings' selector: a loose reading (same owner, or every offering) would sweep in offerings outside SVC_041, including the 19 others owned by USER_004; the count already in repair_in_progress outside SVC_041 must stay at its seed value of 7

Verify Service Offering Status 1.evidence: SVCOFF_050 is the only offering under SVC_041; the requirement tests the same row through the business_service selector

Verify Notification.evidence: the owner's email is right (USER_004); INC_026 is the only high-priority new or in_progress incident on the service, which matches 'referencing the high priority nature of the issue'; carried as requirement 3 with the id anchor added

notes:
Merged from two independent passes. The passes agreed on all four requirements (tables, rows, cells, SQL, expected counts) and on all three dispositions, so there is no disagreement to log; the only differences were in the assumption wording (A counted 3 in_progress incidents on SVC_041, B 6 new or in_progress; both are right on the seed and both counts are recorded in requirement 1). The branch condition is sensitive to the reading of 'active or in-progress': 9 incidents on SVC_041 are unresolved but exactly 3 have status in_progress, so an agent counting only in_progress would (wrongly, by the benchmark's reading) take the 'proceed' branch. 'Treat this situation as resolved from a service perspective, even if some incident details are still pending' is read as having no database effect: no tool writes incidents, and the policy's resolution rules would forbid resolving them without a resolution code and notes; the service status is already fixed by the branch as repair_in_progress. The suspension itself (non-operational or retired) is excluded by requirement 1's exact status, so no separate stay is written for it. The notification requirement anchors on NOTIF_031; if the agent sent a second alert for INC_068 (high, on_hold) first, the anchored copy would be at NOTIF_032 and this check would miss it.
revised: the boundary stay's selector repeated status = 'repair_in_progress', which its cells already carry; the selector now names only the offerings outside SVC_041 and the status stays in cells (same query, same count of 7).
